hgl_proposal: Defaults use the enclosing declaration binding closure and existing generic context, excluding ordinary instance fields and formal argument values. Preserve existing required-constant/cold phase and ownership contracts; no new numeric reification or generic-parameter defaults.
reasoning: Python defaults use the defining scope and are evaluated once; ordinary formal values are not present at definition. A same-spelled outer value can supply a default.
C++ default argument lookup includes earlier formal names, which shadow outer names, but those formals cannot be potentially evaluated. Unevaluated sizeof can mention the formal.
C++ template values are distinct from ordinary function parameters and can bind a function default after specialization. HGL generic value reification is not inferred from this.
C++ ordinary defaults evaluate at each omitted call, while Python captures at definition.

Python class namespace can supply an earlier field class value; C++ default member initialization can read the earlier field of the constructed instance. Neither surface licenses HGL default reads of instance fields.
scope: Conventional ordinary Python/C++ default name binding and evaluation; evidence informs an explicitly chosen HGL declaration-closure rule but does not define HGL semantics.
